[spoiler=[b][i]Beneath the Tides[/b][/i]]
In late March of 2028, several Jomslandic survey vessels were conducting routine seabed mapping beyond the usual shipping lanes when they detected something impossible. The radar detected geometric formations beneath nearly three hundred meters of water. At first, they were dismissed as unusual rock structures until the scans sharpened. The scans showed the remains of houses, roads, and even a temple.
Within 2 weeks, the Althing authorized a deep-sea expedition. The research vessel [i]Yogrim II[/i] was sent to the site, its hull groaning against the cold waves. Below it, a small research submarine dives into the darkness. Inside, the crew watches in silence as the floodlights pierce the abyss. Soon the first walls emerge. Ancient stone structures as well as a long road stretch into the darkness, lined with collapsed buildings. A small harbor, still intact, though its piers now cradle nothing but silt. In the supposed town center stands what could only be a hall. The roof was collapsed, but its stone structure was still intact. This was no unknown settlement.
Preliminary analysis suggests that the ruins predate the first Commonwealth yet somewhat match architectural style from the early first Commonwealth. Some markings recovered from sonar imaging resemble ancient runic scripts of unknown origin. The official statement calls it [i]Site DK-4E200[/i]. But the crew has already given it another name: Bromjunaar
As the submarine moves deeper into the ruins, its cameras catch unexpected movement. A door, shifting slightly in the current. Moments later, the pilot reports a sudden interference in navigation systems. The compasses spin, the signals begin to distort, and then the lights flicker. Before contact is briefly lost, one final image is transmitted to the surface. It shows a pedestal at the far end of the central hall half-buried into the ground. On top sits a mask, a wooden mask, inexplicably undamaged by the cold sea. Alongside the image an audio signal was received. The signal could only be described as a faint voice whispering in an unknown language: 
[i]Mu fen vulon. Mu fen kos meyz.[/i][/spoiler]
